# `w8-import-q56` — the second donor

Imports Claudette's **Q56 quality battery** into a `corpus/SPEC.md` v1 corpus. Step 5 of the W8
plan, and the critical path since David answered F38 with **front-load donor 2** on 2026-08-08.

```bash
cd harness
cargo run -p w8-import-q56 -- --repo /d/dev/claudette --out ../corpus
#   --only Q08        one task, for iterating
#   --skip-gate       emit without measuring points 1 and 2 — emitter work only
#   --force           regenerate; refuses any task.toml without `# GENERATED by` on line 1
```

> ⚠ **The crate is written but has not been compiled yet.** It was authored while five measured
> repetitions were running on the same box, and a cargo build would have perturbed the wall-clock
> numbers those repetitions exist to settle. First job next session: `cargo test -p w8-import-q56`,
> then add it to the workspace `members` (deliberately left out for the same reason — a manifest
> error would have broken the runs mid-series).

## Why this donor exists in W8 at all

U100 cannot measure operator control. **Creating a new file never fires a permission gate; touching
a file that already exists always does**, whichever edit tool the model reaches for (F39) — and 76
of U100's 90 tasks start from an empty fixture, so ~14 of them can fire a gate at all (F38).

Every one of Q56's 56 tasks ships a non-empty fixture (F40). They are gate-capable *structurally*,
not by luck of which tool the model picks, which also retires F30's tool lottery as a threat to the
measurement. The survey is `research/W8-q56-import.md`; the approved `Q08` field mapping is
`research/W8-corpus-format.md` §A. **Do not re-derive either.**

## Shape

`donor.rs` (extract) → `verify_sh.rs` (rewrite) → `gate.rs` (measure) → `emit.rs` (write).

**Extraction reads `git show <commit>:<path>`, never a working tree.** The donor lives on the
unmerged `battery/q50-quality-corpus` branch at `43d6b34` while Claudette's `main` carries a
different, older A-K battery. Naming a commit is what makes the import reproducible, and it makes
"no donor is edited" a property a program enforces rather than a rule someone remembers. CRLF is
normalised at read even though Q56 is LF today — that class of bug has produced a false difference
four times here (F21, F22, F29, and `w8-run/src/main.rs`).

**`manifest-q50.tsv` is the boundary of the suite, not the directory listing.** The same donor
directory holds the older A-K battery and four `T01`-`T04` tasks. A count other than 56 aborts the
import rather than importing whatever it found.

## The four things worth knowing before reading the code

**1. The verifier rewrite uses shell functions, not search-and-replace.** SPEC §8 wants interpreters
resolved through the environment; the donor hardcodes `python` ×15, `pytest` ×23, `node` ×39,
`cargo` ×14. Rewriting call sites textually would have to tell a real invocation from the same word
inside a heredoc — and those heredocs are the hidden reviewer tests, the most load-bearing bytes in
the donor. A function named `cargo` intercepts every execution and edits no text at all, so
everything below the prelude stays byte-identical:

```bash
cargo(){ command "${CARGO:-cargo}" "$@"; }   # `command` bypasses the function, so this dispatches
```

**2. A missing toolchain prints `INVALID`, not `FAIL`** — a deliberate strictening over the donor,
whose README says a missing toolchain does not skip its tasks but fails them, silently costing up to
19 points. That conflates "the verifier did not run" with "the artifact is wrong", which is F35, and
it is the whole reason SPEC §8 has a third verdict the donor contract does not. Interpreters are
probed **by executing**: Windows' Store alias shim `python3.exe` is on PATH, `command -v` finds it,
and it prints an advert instead of running code (F27).

**3. Point 1's pre-state is the donor's untouched fixture, not §9's generated stub.** Every Q56
fixture compiles and passes its visible happy-path tests while failing the hidden reviewer tests
injected at grade time — which is exactly the state the null-implementation stub was invented to
simulate for U100 (F19). The stronger input is the free one here, and it means §9's stub vocabulary
(python and node only) never needs a rust, ts or shell case.

**4. The gate is re-run rather than trusted.** The donor's own `gate_q50.sh` already refuses a task
entry to the manifest unless the untouched fixture FAILs and fixture+refsol PASSes, so both points
are pre-satisfied by construction (F45). They are measured anyway, against the **rewritten**
verifier, because `verifier = "rewritten"` is SPEC §9's authoritative column — and because U100
scored 79 of 80 sound at point 1 and F8 still found a verifier passing an intact SQL injection.

## What blocks 8 of the 56

**F47: SPEC §3's `lang` vocabulary has no `shell`**, and 8 Q56 tasks are shell. The vocabulary is
closed in the loader (`w8-corpus/src/model.rs`), so those tasks are a load rejection, and a rejected
task rejects the whole corpus. The importer **refuses them by name with the reason** and imports the
other 48; it does not map them onto `mixed`, which means "several languages in one task" and would
put a false value in a field whose entire purpose is to be checkable. The fix is a one-word
amendment and it is David's to make.

## Two sequencing constraints, both learned the hard way

- **`expected_tasks` must stay out of `suites/q56/suite.toml` until all 56 are emitted.** The loader
  checks it against the tree, and a rejected suite rejects the whole corpus — so a placeholder `56`
  beside one task directory stops `w8-run` loading **u100** as well. The importer prints the reminder
  when, and only when, the set is complete.
- **A second suite makes `--suite` mandatory for `w8-run`.** Any script that omitted it starts
  failing the moment this suite appears. Neither is a defect; both are guards working. Together they
  mean the q56 tree cannot appear under `corpus/` while runs are in flight against u100.
